leads.title: Section 175 of the Reich Criminal Code (Reichsstrafgesetzbuch)
leads.documents: Criminalization of homosexual acts between men used for Nazi persecution; article states several thousand men sentenced under it, about 6,000 interned to camps with high death rate; postwar retention in West Germany with 50,000 convictions 1945-1969, reforms 1969/1973, full repeal 1994.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'section 175 of the Reichs Criminal Code' and 'Sections 175 and 175a from the Nazi era'; no URL visible in provided text

leads.title: Section 175a
leads.documents: Aggravated homosexual offences provision; continued application in GDR after 1950 and retained in Nazi-era version in FRG (West Germany) until reforms; shows enforcement continuity.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Section 175a continued to be applied' and 'stuck to the versions of Sections 175 and 175a'; no URL visible

leads.title: Section 151 - GDR Penal Code (1968)
leads.documents: East German law making same-sex sexual acts with minors punishable for both women and men; documents differential age-of-consent regime in East Berlin, deleted with effect July 1, 1989.
leads.detail: Cited as 'made same-sex sexual acts with minors a punishable offense for both women and men in § 151' enacted 1968, deleted July 1, 1989; no URL visible

leads.title: 2017 Rehabilitation and Compensation for Section 175 victims
leads.documents: Legal rehabilitation of men punished under pre-1969 broader version of Section 175; compensation of 3,000 euros plus 1,500 euros 'for each year of detention suffered' for those actually convicted; documents redress machinery and lifelong employment/housing consequences.
leads.detail: Cited as 'were not rehabilitated until 2017' with compensation amounts quoted; formal act name not given in excerpt, no URL visible

leads.title: Memorial to Homosexuals Persecuted Under Nazism - Berlin Tiergarten
leads.documents: State memorialization of anti-gay enforcement; located across Ebertstrasse from Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe in Grosse Tiergarten, near Sinti and Roma memorial; documents official recognition of persecution site.
leads.detail: Described as 'across in the Große Tiergarten across Ebertstraße from Peter Eisenman's Memorial'; no URL visible

leads.title: Schwules Museum (Gay Museum), Berlin - opened 1985
leads.documents: World's first gay museum, 'institution dedicated to preserving, exhibiting, and discovering gay and lesbian history, art, and culture'; institutional rights-memory infrastructure in Berlin.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In 1985, Berlin opened the world's first gay museum, otherwise known as the Schwules Museum'; no URL visible

leads.title: Eldorado: Everything the Nazis Hate - historian Klaus Mueller
leads.documents: Historical argument that contemporary queer Berlin is not a continuation of 1920s due to Nazi destruction of Hirschfeld's Institute for Sexual Science, research, first gender-affirming surgeries documentation; quote: 'That really was lost. No names. No memory. Nothing.'
leads.detail: Attributed to 'historian Klaus Mueller argues in Eldorado: Everything the Nazis Hate'; no URL visible

leads.title: Checkpoint.BLN sexual health clinic
leads.documents: Berlin harm-reduction / health enforcement machinery; offers counselling and support for chemsex and education on harm reduction, drug testing services at festivals/clubs cited as city forefront policy.
leads.detail: Cited as 'sexual health clinics like Checkpoint.BLN offer counselling and support for those navigating chem sex'; no URL visible

leads.title: Crime Scene Berlin: The Night Life Killer (documentary)
leads.documents: Documented incident series: GHB-related murders in Friedrichshain nightlife, first death recorded at bar Grosse-Freiheit 114, GHB dosage lethality, Berghain bans, bar signage warnings; linked to period of increased homophobia and caution around darkrooms/drinks.
leads.detail: Cited as 'according to specialists interviewed in the documentary Crime Scene Berlin: The Night Life Killer' plus owner statement from 2024; no URL visible

leads.title: White Terror: A True Story of Murders, Bombings and a Far-Right Campaign to Rid Germany of Immigrants - Jacob Kushner
leads.documents: Documented far-right / neo-Nazi violent attacks on migrants; cited to contextualize xenophobia and discrimination faced by queer migrants (especially non-western/non-white) in Berlin and rise of neo-nazism.
leads.detail: Cited as 'A case of this is documented in Jacob Kushner's White Terror...'; no URL visible
